name: .45 Auto Composite
description:
The .45 Auto has been around long enough that arguing about it is a personality type. The 'Composite' designation refers to the updated projectile construction that became standard sometime around 2150 — a layered copper-polymer jacket over a dense tungsten-alloy core, replacing the old lead-core designs that became environmentally restricted after the Lake Michigan Reclamation Accords. The result is a round with the same wide, subsonic profile that made the original famous, but with better barrier penetration and reduced splash hazard in close-quarters environments. It still hits like a thrown cinder block. It still makes big holes. That hasn't changed.

In GLMZ 2200, .45 Auto Composite is the round of choice for a certain kind of professional — mid-tier fixers, veteran Arcturus Civil Security contractors who bought their sidearms after service and never switched, and the kind of Tier 2 shop boss who wants stopping power they can actually afford to practice with. It's not cheap, but it's not boutique. Kovash Munitions and Drevko Arms both produce it in commercial and contract grades. The commercial grade comes in dented steel cartons with printed lot numbers. The contract grade comes in vacuum-sealed polymer tubes that cost three times as much and perform maybe five percent better. Most people buy the dented cartons.
compatibility_note: Compatible with full-size and compact pistols chambered in .45 ACP, including the Drevko D-45 platform and older Halverson service pistols. Also feeds in some submachine gun platforms chambered for the round. Wide availability across Tier 1–3 markets.
reliability_note: Brass-cased gunpowder propulsion with composite projectile construction. Extremely reliable across temperature ranges and fouling conditions. The composite jacket reduces barrel wear compared to older lead-core loads. No electronic dependency; functions in EMP environments and adverse weather without modification.
